title: m-pseudo-coherence in distinguished triangles of ring complexes
statement: Let $R$ be a ring and $m$ an integer, and let $D(R)$ be the derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] of the abelian category of $R$-modules. Call an object $C$ of $D(R)$ $m$-pseudo-coherent if there are a bounded complex $E^\bullet$ of finite free $R$-modules and a morphism $E^\bullet\to C$ in $D(R)$ inducing isomorphisms $H^i(E^\bullet)\to H^i(C)$ for $i>m$ and a surjection $H^m(E^\bullet)\to H^m(C)$. Let $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$ be a distinguished triangle in $D(R)$. If $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $B$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent; if $A$ and $C$ are $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $B$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent; and if $B$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent and $C$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, then $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent.

proof.text: For the first clause, choose a bounded finite-free witness $P^\bullet\to A$ which is an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i>m+1$ and surjective on $H^{m+1}$, and a bounded finite-free witness $\beta:E^\bullet\to B$ which is an isomorphism on $H^i$ for $i>m$ and surjective on $H^m$. Replace $P^\bullet$ by its brutal truncation $\sigma_{\ge m+1}P^\bullet$ (terms of degree $\ge m+1$): its $H^i$ agrees with that of $P^\bullet$ for $i>m+1$ and $H^{m+1}(\sigma_{\ge m+1}P^\bullet)=\ker d^{m+1}\to H^{m+1}(P^\bullet)$ is surjective, so the witness conditions are unchanged and now $P^i=0$ for $i<m+1$, in particular for $i<m$. Apply [lem-pc-ring-derived-map-lift] with $n=m$, $\alpha=\beta:E^\bullet\to B$ and the composite $P^\bullet\to A\to B$: it gives a chain map $\gamma:P^\bullet\to E^\bullet$ with $\beta\circ Q(\gamma)$ equal to $P^\bullet\to A\to B$ in $D(R)$. The cone construction in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] gives a bounded finite-free complex $Q^\bullet=C(\gamma)^\bullet$ and a distinguished triangle $P^\bullet\to E^\bullet\to Q^\bullet\to P^\bullet[1]$; by (TR3) of [def-weil-triangulated-category] the commutative square extends to a morphism of distinguished triangles to $A\to B\to C\to A[1]$. Take the long exact cohomology sequences of both triangles [lem-sf-derived-homology-long-exact]; the morphism of triangles gives a commutative ladder between them [lem-weil-pbc-derived-cohomology-ladder]. For every $i>m$, consider the five terms $H^i(P)\to H^i(E)\to H^i(Q)\to H^{i+1}(P)\to H^{i+1}(E)$ over the corresponding terms for $A,B,C$: the first vertical map is surjective ($i\ge m+1$), the second, fourth and fifth are isomorphisms ($i>m$, $i+1>m+1$), so the five-lemma [lem-weil-pbc-five-lemma] gives $H^i(Q)\cong H^i(C)$. At $i=m$, consider the four terms $H^m(E)\to H^m(Q)\to H^{m+1}(P)\to H^{m+1}(E)$: the vertical maps on $H^m(E)$ and $H^{m+1}(P)$ are surjective and the one on $H^{m+1}(E)$ is an isomorphism, hence a monomorphism, so the four lemma [lem-pc-four-lemma-epi] gives surjectivity $H^m(Q)\twoheadrightarrow H^m(C)$. Thus $Q^\bullet\to C$ is the required $m$-pseudo-coherent witness for $C$.

For the second clause, rotate twice to the distinguished triangle $C\to A[1]\to B[1]\to C[1]$. From $A$ being $m$-pseudo-coherent, the identity $H^i(A[1])=H^{i+1}(A)$ gives that $A[1]$ is $(m-1)$-pseudo-coherent; $C$ is $(m-1+1)$-pseudo-coherent because it is $m$-pseudo-coherent. Applying the first clause with index $m-1$ gives that $B[1]$ is $(m-1)$-pseudo-coherent, and shifting back gives that $B$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent. For the third clause, rotate to $B\to C\to A[1]\to B[1]$, apply the first clause with index $m$ to obtain that $A[1]$ is $m$-pseudo-coherent, and use $H^i(A[1])=H^{i+1}(A)$ to conclude that $A$ is $(m+1)$-pseudo-coherent. Rotation preserves distinguished triangles by the triangulated structure in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].
